key_insight: Harmful behaviors in LLMs are concentrated in a compact, unified set of model weights — targeted pruning of that subnetwork causally reduces harmful outputs while largely preserving other capabilities.
problem_solved: Investigates why alignment is brittle (jailbreaks and emergent misalignment) by testing whether harmfulness has a coherent, separable internal organization that can be intervened on causally.
method: Use targeted weight pruning as a causal intervention to identify and remove weights that drive harmful outputs.
Evaluate effects across jailbreak prompts and models fine-tuned on narrow domains to test generalization of the intervention.
Perform layer-wise and ablation analyses to show the harmfulness mechanism is distinct from other language capabilities.
impact: Demonstrates a concrete, auditable lever (weight-level interventions) for reducing harmful outputs, informing more precise mitigation strategies and robustness checks for alignment.
visual_elements: Schematic of a transformer with a highlighted 'harmfulness subnetwork' being pruned (scissors icon) and before/after example outputs.
Line chart: harmfulness metric vs percentage of targeted weights pruned (showing a steep decline).
Layer-wise heatmap or bar chart indicating concentration of harmfulness-related weights across layers/neurons.
Side-by-side text example comparing an original harmful response to the safe response after pruning.
paper_title: Large Language Models Generate Harmful Content Using a Distinct, Unified Mechanism
paper_authors: Hadas Orgad, Boyi Wei, Kaden Zheng, Martin Wattenberg, Peter Henderson
